review.tagline: Cuts token use in coding agents with terse replies and compressed inputs
review.summary: Caveman is a CLI and skill set that reduces token use in coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and OpenCode. It shortens agent replies, compresses logs, JSON, CSV and test output before the model reads them, and can route each request to a model and effort level through a free account. Reported results include 33.2% fewer input tokens over 54 Claude Code runs and an interim 54% cost cut for Auto on 85 tasks.
review.audience: Developers paying for Claude Code, Codex or similar agents who want lower spend
strengths: One npx command sets up 30+ agents; runs locally with your own keys
README lists losing cases: HTML input 9.9% worse, grep-defs loses to bare grep
Each part can be switched off separately; the skill installs alone
Cited by Adobe Research paper, JetBrains A/B on 86 tasks, Elastic blog
weaknesses: Auto routing needs a Caveman account; its benchmark is interim and half complete
Terse output saves nothing on per-request billing such as GitHub Copilot
Rules cost about 1,160 input tokens; output benchmarks used older 3.1.0 rules
No HTML compressor yet; Blocks is pre-release (v0.1.0-rc.5), Python only
needs: Models: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Aider
